subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Sheehan Syndrome

steps.tx: **Sheehan syndrome** refers to postpartum anterior pituitary necrosis provoked by catastrophic obstetric haemorrhage and profound hypovolaemic shock during delivery. During pregnancy, the anterior pituitary gland hypertrophies up to twice its normal volume without an increase in its vascular supply. When severe postpartum haemorrhage occurs, severe arterial hypotension triggers intense vasospasm and microthrombi within the low-pressure hypophyseal-portal capillary plexus. This causes ischaemic necrosis of seventy-five percent or more of anterior pituitary parenchymal tissue.
steps.say: Sheehan syndrome results from ischaemic anterior pituitary necrosis following massive postpartum haemorrhage. The hypertrophied pituitary gland collapses into avascular infarction when severe hypotension shuts down the low-pressure portal capillary circulation.

left.title: Anterior Pituitary Vulnerability
points: Doubles in volume during normal pregnancy
Prone to ischaemic infarction during shock

right.title: Posterior Pituitary Resilience
points: Direct arterial blood supply from internal carotid

steps.tx: **Failure of lactation** in the immediate postpartum puerperium represents the earliest, most characteristic clinical harbinger of Sheehan syndrome. Destruction of pituitary lactotroph cells produces absolute prolactin deficiency, preventing physiological breast engorgement and milk synthesis. The woman is entirely unable to breastfeed her newborn. Months later, persistent secondary amenorrhoea supervenes due to gonadotroph destruction and deficient luteinizing hormone and follicle-stimulating hormone secretion, signaling irreversible hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis collapse.
steps.say: The earliest clinical sign is the sudden inability to lactate after delivery due to prolactin deficiency. Months later, failure of menses to return despite not breastfeeding confirms anterior pituitary failure.

vis.title: Sequential Clinical Emergence of Endocrine Deficits

nodes.label: Failure of Lactation
nodes.sub: Prolactin lack causes agalactia in puerperium

steps.tx: **Panhypopituitarism** develops insidiously as hormone deficiencies unfold in a classic chronological order: growth hormone and prolactin fail first, followed sequentially by luteinizing hormone, follicle-stimulating hormone, thyroid-stimulating hormone, and adrenocorticotropic hormone. Progressive hypopituitarism leads to dry, prematurely aged skin, fine perioral wrinkling, cold intolerance, profound asthenia, bradycardia, and orthostatic hypotension. Because posterior pituitary vascular supply arises directly from internal carotid arteries, diabetes insipidus occurs in fewer than five percent of cases.
steps.say: Panhypopituitarism develops sequentially, losing growth hormone and prolactin first, followed by gonadotropins, TSH, and ACTH. Patients develop cold intolerance, lethargy, bradycardia, and orthostatic hypotension, while diabetes insipidus remains exceptionally rare.

vis.title: Sequential Pituitary Hormone Deficits and Clinical Signs

steps.tx: **Axillary hair loss** and complete loss of pubic hair (trichotillomania-like depilation) constitute cardinal physical examination findings in established Sheehan syndrome. Loss of adrenal androgens driven by ACTH deficiency, coupled with ovarian failure from absent gonadotropins, causes complete involution of secondary sexual hair. Physical inspection also demonstrates marked regression of breast tissue, urogenital mucosal atrophy causing severe dyspareunia, and distinctive alabaster-like cutaneous pallor resulting from combined anaemia and lack of melanocyte-stimulating hormone.
steps.say: Loss of pubic and axillary hair is a classic physical sign, driven by combined adrenal androgen and ovarian hormone deficiency. Look also for breast atrophy, urogenital dryness, and pale alabaster skin.

right.title: Secondary Adrenal Failure (Sheehan)
points: Low ACTH fails to stimulate melanocytes

steps.tx: **Empty sella** sign on high-resolution sagittal cranial magnetic resonance imaging provides definitive radiological confirmation of chronic Sheehan syndrome. In the acute necrotic phase, imaging reveals an enlarged, non-enhancing, infarcted pituitary gland with surrounding ring enhancement. Over subsequent years, necrotic pituitary parenchyma undergoes autolysis and shrinkage, allowing the arachnoid space to herniate downward through the diaphragma sellae. Cerebrospinal fluid fills the sella turcica, flattening a thin sliver of residual pituitary tissue against the floor.
steps.say: Magnetic resonance imaging confirms Sheehan syndrome by displaying an empty sella. The necrotic pituitary tissue atrophies over time, allowing cerebrospinal fluid to fill the sella turcica and compress the residual gland against the bone floor.

vis.title: Radiological Evolution of the Sella Turcica

nodes.label: Tissue Autolysis
nodes.sub: Parenchymal shrinkage over months to years

nodes.label: Empty Sella
nodes.sub: Flattened rim of residual pituitary tissue

steps.tx: **Corticosteroid replacement** must unconditionally precede the initiation of thyroid hormone replacement in patients with Sheehan syndrome. Administering levothyroxine before hydrocortisone accelerates hepatic metabolic clearance of circulating cortisol while increasing basal metabolic tissue demands. In a patient with compromised adrenal reserve, this precipitous drop in available cortisol triggers a fatal, life-threatening acute addisonian crisis with refractory cardiovascular collapse. Hydrocortisone fifteen to twenty milligrams daily is initiated first, followed several days later by cautious levothyroxine titration.
steps.say: Never start levothyroxine before hydrocortisone in Sheehan syndrome. Thyroid hormone accelerates cortisol breakdown, which will trigger a fatal adrenal crisis in an un-supplemented patient. Always replace steroids first.

vis.title: Critical Hierarchy of Hormone Replacement Therapy

nodes.label: Hydrocortisone First
nodes.sub: 15 to 20 mg daily in divided morning doses

nodes.label: Levothyroxine Second
nodes.sub: Start 50 mcg daily after glucocorticoid cover

nodes.label: Steroid Safety Rule
nodes.sub: Double glucocorticoid dose during acute illness

steps.tx: **Hormone replacement therapy** incorporating cyclical physiological estrogen and progestogen is essential in premenopausal women with Sheehan syndrome to prevent severe premature osteoporotic fractures and alleviate urogenital atrophy. Conjugated equine estrogen 0.625 mg daily or transdermal estradiol patches are combined with micronized progesterone 200 mg for twelve days per month to induce scheduled withdrawal bleeding and protect the endometrium. In addition to preserving bone mineral density, cyclical therapy restores secondary sexual characteristics, libido, and well-being.
steps.say: Premenopausal women require physiological estrogen and progestin replacement to preserve bone density, maintain secondary sexual characteristics, and protect the endometrium from unopposed proliferation.

vis.title: Comprehensive Replacement Protocols in Panhypopituitarism
rows: Serum free T4 in upper half of normal range
Symptom relief, bone mineral density DEXA
Serum IGF-1 levels in age-matched range

steps.tx: **Ovulation induction** for women with Sheehan syndrome seeking pregnancy cannot be achieved with clomiphene citrate because endogenous hypothalamic-pituitary gonadotroph function is permanently destroyed. Instead, successful conception requires exogenous gonadotropin therapy, administering daily subcutaneous injections of recombinant follicle-stimulating hormone or human menopausal gonadotropins to promote ovarian follicular growth. Once the dominant follicle reaches eighteen millimetres on transvaginal ultrasonography, human chorionic gonadotropin is injected to trigger ovulation, followed by luteal phase progesterone support.
steps.say: Clomiphene citrate will not work for ovulation induction in Sheehan syndrome because the pituitary gland cannot produce gonadotropins. Exogenous gonadotropin injections containing FSH and LH are mandatory to stimulate follicles.

left.title: Clomiphene Citrate Ineffective
points: Acts by blocking hypothalamic estrogen feedback
Cannot elicit LH/FSH release from necrotic gland

right.title: Exogenous Gonadotropins Required
points: Recombinant FSH or hMG directly stimulates ovary
hCG injection administered to trigger oocyte release
